samples.summary: Vacuous assertion: "a read-only mount still reads presence" only checks `Array.isArray(...)`
samples.evidence: `expect(Array.isArray(store.getPresences())).toBe(true)` holds whether or not the read half of presence works — an implementation that gated reads and returned `[]` passes identically. The sibling docs test (`tests/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store-read-only.test.ts`, `a read-only mount still reads peer presence`) explicitly calls this out and seeds an actual peer via `seedPeerPresence` before asserting the peer comes back; this spreadsheet twin does not, so the claimed 'one-directional gate' property is not actually covered for `YorkieStore`.

samples.summary: `sideTokenInjector`'s no-fallback rule (per-side env secret, never the running shell's JWT_SECRET) has no test
samples.evidence: The function's entire reason for existing is that a service token grants read/write on *every* document of the deployment that minted it, so defaulting the target side to `process.env.JWT_SECRET` would ship deployment A's all-documents credential to deployment B. Nothing exercises it: there are no `*.spec.ts`/`*.test.ts` under `packages/backend/scripts` (glob returned nothing), and no backend spec imports `copy-yorkie-documents`. `auth.service.spec.ts` covers `signYorkieServiceToken`/`yorkieServiceTokenInjector`/`yorkieServiceTokenInjectorFromEnv`, but never the two-sided selection. A regression that reintroduces a fallback would ship silently.

samples.summary: The new `readOnly` guard on `onActivePageChange` is untested, although a new test file for this very module was added
samples.evidence: `packages/frontend/tests/app/files/pdf-collab-provider.test.tsx` (added in this diff) only asserts `initialRoot` is `{}` vs `{comments:{}}`. Grepping `onActivePageChange|activePage` across `packages/frontend/tests/app/files/pdf-collab.test.tsx` returns no matches, so the `if (readOnly || !doc || ...)` early-return — the guard the diff says prevents wedging a viewer's whole sync on first page scroll — has no coverage anywhere.

samples.summary: `readOnlyMount` presence-broadcast guards in slides-view and board-view have no test
samples.evidence: Both `slides-view.tsx`'s `broadcast = () => { if (readOnlyMount) return; ... }` and `board-view.tsx`'s `onSelectionChange(() => { if (readOnly) return; store.updatePresence(...) })` are new guards whose failure (per the diff's own reasoning) wedges a viewer's sync on the first click. Grepping `updatePresence|broadcast|onSelectionChange` under `packages/frontend/tests` matches only slides toolbar/format-panel and the slides store tests; none covers these call sites. The analogous store-level gates (YorkieStore, YorkieDocStore) do get tests, so the pattern is partially covered but these two mounts are not.
searchedFor: Grep readOnly in packages/frontend/tests (9 files, none board/slides view)

samples.evidence: The new engine backstop is covered by `packages/sheets/test/view/spreadsheet-readonly-recalc.test.ts`, but nothing asserts that sheet-view actually passes `!readOnly` (or `new YorkieStore(doc, tabId, readOnly)`). No frontend test under `packages/frontend/tests` references sheet-view's remote-sync path. Contained because the engine refuses the write anyway, so a regression here costs a wasted pass rather than a write.

samples.summary: `NotesView`'s new `readOnly ? readOnlyNoteStore(raw) : raw` wrapping is not covered; the one new test that mounts it mocks NotesView away
samples.evidence: `readOnlyNoteStore` itself (packages/notes/src/store/read-only.test.ts) and `initialize()`'s wrapping (packages/notes/src/view/editor.test.ts) are well covered, but the frontend mount's own wrap is not: `packages/frontend/src/app/shared/shared-notes-layout.test.tsx` replaces `@/app/notes/notes-view` with a stub (`vi.mock("@/app/notes/notes-view", …)`) that only records props, so it can only assert `viewProps.current.readOnly === true`, never that the store handed to the engine is guarded. Impact is limited by `initialize()` wrapping independently and the wrapper being idempotent.

samples.summary: `yorkieServiceTokenInjectorFromEnv`'s success path (and its `YORKIE_TOKEN_EXPIRES_IN` handling) is untested — only the missing-secret branch is
samples.evidence: auth.service.spec.ts's 'hands back no injector when there is no secret to sign with' calls `yorkieServiceTokenInjectorFromEnv('')` and asserts `undefined` + the warning. Nothing calls it with a secret, so the two migration scripts' actual credential (does it sign? with which expiry?) has no coverage; a regression returning an unusable or never-expiring token would pass.

samples.summary: YorkieService's missing-`JWT_SECRET` branch (undefined injector + warning) is untested
samples.evidence: `createMockConfigService()` in yorkie.service.spec.ts always returns `JWT_SECRET`, and the two new tests only assert the signed, scoped token. No test constructs the service with a bare config to check that `authTokenInjector` is `undefined` (rather than a function signing with `undefined`) and that the warn fires — the branch the doc comment says tools and tests actually hit.

samples.summary: Recalc read-only test runs the prototype method against a hand-built context, so it cannot catch the mount ever failing to set `_readOnly`
samples.evidence: The test builds `{_readOnly, sheet, worksheet}` itself and calls `Spreadsheet.prototype.recalculateCrossSheetFormulas.call(ctx)`. It proves the branch body, but asserts nothing about a real `Spreadsheet` constructed read-only actually having `_readOnly === true`; if the constructor/`setReadOnly` path stopped propagating the flag, these tests stay green while a viewer's mount resumes persisting recalculated cache values. The file acknowledges the technique but the coupling gap is real.

samples.summary: No round-trip test that a *scoped* service token's `key` survives verification
samples.evidence: The new tests mint `signYorkieServiceToken('access-secret','10m')` with no key, and yorkie.service.spec verifies the keyed token with a bare `new JwtService()` rather than through `AuthService.verifyYorkieToken`. `decideService` in the controller reads `identity.key` off the verified payload; no test joins the minting-with-key and verifying halves, though the controller tests supply the key directly.

finding.summary: `sideTokenInjector`'s no-fallback rule (per-side env secret, never the running shell's JWT_SECRET) has no test
finding.evidence: The function's entire reason for existing is that a service token grants read/write on *every* document of the deployment that minted it, so defaulting the target side to `process.env.JWT_SECRET` would ship deployment A's all-documents credential to deployment B. Nothing exercises it: there are no `*.spec.ts`/`*.test.ts` under `packages/backend/scripts` (glob returned nothing), and no backend spec imports `copy-yorkie-documents`. `auth.service.spec.ts` covers `signYorkieServiceToken`/`yorkieServiceTokenInjector`/`yorkieServiceTokenInjectorFromEnv`, but never the two-sided selection. A regression that reintroduces a fallback would ship silently.

verdict.reason: `sideTokenInjector` (packages/backend/scripts/copy-yorkie-documents.ts:40-54) implements the per-side, no-fallback secret rule and is used at lines 258/262, but nothing exercises it. Glob of packages/backend/scripts shows no test files; repo-wide grep for SOURCE_JWT|TARGET_JWT returns only the script itself (5 hits, no test); repo-wide grep for `sideTokenInjector` returns only the script and a docs TODO; the only test-file hit for `copy-yorkie-documents` is scripts/test/verify-entropy.test.mjs:122,175, where the path is a literal string inside a fake file index for a link-resolver test and the script is never imported. The adjacent coverage in packages/backend/src/auth/auth.service.spec.ts:110-146 tests only the shared helper (`yorkieServiceTokenInjector(undefined|'')` -> undefined, the FromEnv warn path, foreign-secret rejection) and never the two-sided env selection; `src/yorkie/yorkie-service-token.ts` has no spec of its own, and no spec asserts on the script's source text. The repo's own review log at docs/tasks/active/20260907-notes-share-toolbar-todo.md:96-101 explicitly marks `sideTokenInjector` as deferred coverage. Under the test-adequacy rubric this is a changed guard behavior with no meaningful test, whose silent regression (reintroducing a fallback to process.env.JWT_SECRET) would send one deployment's all-documents service credential to another deployment's Yorkie server — a guard that would weaken silently on the exact path an operator takes when they omit a flag.

mergedFrom.summary: New read-only early-return in `Spreadsheet.recalculateCrossSheetFormulas` has no test in packages/sheets

finding.summary: `Spreadsheet.recalculateCrossSheetFormulas` read-only early-return is untested, and so is `sheet-view`'s `runRemoteSync(!readOnly)` gate
finding.evidence: The diff adds `if (this._readOnly) { this.worksheet.render(); return; }` to `Spreadsheet.recalculateCrossSheetFormulas` and calls it the engine-level backstop ('so neither this call site nor a future one can leak it'). `grep recalculateCrossSheetFormulas packages/sheets` shows tests only for `Sheet.recalculateCrossSheetFormulas` (test/sheet/cross-sheet-*.test.ts), none constructing a read-only `Spreadsheet`; the only read-only view test, test/view/worksheet-readonly-editing.test.ts, covers `finishEditing` only. Frontend-side, `runRemoteSync(!readOnly)` and `scheduleRemoteSync(readOnly ? false : …)` in sheet-view.tsx have no test either (no sheet-view test file). A regression re-enables a viewer's recalc write, which the webhook refuses and which wedges that viewer's sync — the exact failure this change exists to prevent.

verdict.reason: The read-only early return in `Spreadsheet.recalculateCrossSheetFormulas` (packages/sheets/src/view/spreadsheet.ts:990-998) IS tested by packages/sheets/test/view/spreadsheet-readonly-recalc.test.ts, which the reviewer missed. The test invokes the real prototype method (`Spreadsheet.prototype.recalculateCrossSheetFormulas`, lines 23-27) against a hand-built `this`, and asserts branch-distinguishing outcomes: on a read-only context `sheet.recalculateCrossSheetFormulas` is not called while `worksheet.render()` is called once (lines 47-58), on a writable context both are called once (lines 38-45), and with no attached sheet nothing happens (lines 60-67). The method body is not mocked — only its collaborators — so deleting the `if (this._readOnly)` gate would fail the test. The file matches vitest's default include and packages/sheets/vite.config.ts uses defaults, so it runs. The finding's secondary half is accurate (no sheet-view test exists for `runRemoteSync(!readOnly)` at packages/frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/sheet-view.tsx:1317 and 1331), but per the code comment at sheet-view.tsx:1301-1311 and the engine doc comment, that call site is an optimization above the tested engine gate — a regression there cannot leak a viewer write, so the residual gap is contained and does not sustain the claimed major user-visible/sync-wedging impact.
